# Ty1 insertion quantification at tRNA genes

```{r load-library-depth-data}
read_counts <- readxl::read_xlsx(path = p.library_size_file) %>% 
  pivot_longer(where(is.numeric),
               names_to = "norm_type",
               values_to = "seq_library_size")
```

```{r load-trna-locations}
trna_df <- load_trna_region_data_frame(p.bt.trna_bed_path)
```

Loaded `r nrow(trna_df)` tRNA gene locations.

```{r load-coverage-data}
# TEST:
# tmp <- .load_coverage_matrix(file.path(params$data_dir, p.bt.input_trna_coverage_file_names)[4]) %>%
#   .separate_strand_and_proximity(index = names(p.bt.input_trna_coverage_file_names)[4]) %>%
#   .add_trna_names() %>%
#   .pivot_coverage_longer_and_aggregate()

bt.cov_df <- purrr::imap(
  .x = setNames(
    file.path(p.bt.trna_cov_dir, p.bt.input_trna_coverage_file_names),
    names(p.bt.input_trna_coverage_file_names)),
  .f = load_coverage_data_frame,
  trna_feat_df = trna_df) %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows()

missing <- trna_df %>% 
  dplyr::filter(! trna.name %in% unique(dplyr::pull(bt.cov_df, trna.name)))

if (nrow(missing) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste(nrow(missing), " tRNA genes were not found in the tRNA coverage dataset:",
          paste(missing$trna.name, collapse = ", "),
          sep = "")
  )
}
```

```{r transform-data}
bt.cov_df <- normalise_sequencing_library_coverage(
  df = bt.cov_df,
  read_counts = read_counts
)

libs_missing <- filter(bt.cov_df, is.na(coverage.norm)) %>% 
  distinct(library) %>% 
  pull(library)

if (length(libs_missing) >= 1) {
  stop(
    paste("Unable to calculate coverage for libraries",
          paste(libs_missing, collapse = ", "))
  )
}

```

```{r extract-metadata-from-library-names}
bt.cov_df <- extract_metadata_from_library_names(bt.cov_df)
```

```{r define-category-palettes}

metadata_palette_list <- bt.cov_df %>% 
  dplyr::distinct(subunit, strain.type, sugar, group) %>% 
  colour_metadata(
    brewer_palette_name = c("BrBG", "Paired", "Set3", "Spectral"),
    palette_size = 11
  )

subunit_pal_names <- setNames(
  unique(pull(bt.cov_df, subunit)),
  c("Blues", "Greens", "Purples", "Reds")
)
metadata_palette_list[["group"]] <- setNames("#969696", c("WT"))
for (i in seq(1, length(subunit_pal_names))) {
  n <- bt.cov_df %>%
    filter(
      subunit == subunit_pal_names[[i]],
      group != "WT") %>%
    distinct(group) %>%
    colour_metadata(brewer_palette_name = names(subunit_pal_names)[i])
  metadata_palette_list[["group"]] <- c(
    metadata_palette_list[["group"]], n[["group"]]
  )
}



```

## Butterfly plot

```{r plot-butterfly, fig.cap = "Butterfly plot showing the normalised sequencing coverage -- a proxy for the number of Ty1 insertions -- upstream and downstream of a tRNA gene. Sequencing coverage was normalised by the number of reads sequenced for each library. tRNA genes encoded on the mitochondrial chromosome were omitted."}
nucleosome_position_df <- data.frame(
  x = c(860, 685, 510, 335, 160),
  y = 0
)

p.span <- 0.08  # Controls the amount of smoothing for the default loess smoother
# (0.75 by default). Values between 0.08 and 0.05 retain the double-peak.
p.level <- 0.99  # Level of confidence interval to use (0.95 by default).
bt.cov_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit, library, proximity, strand, rel.position) %>%
  summarise(
    coverage.norm = sum(coverage.norm),
    .groups = "keep"
  ) %>% 
  plot_butterfly(annot_df = nucleosome_position_df,
                 trna_feat_df = trna_df,
                 span = p.span,
                 level = p.level,
                 .smooth_se = TRUE,
                 .annot_size = 4)
```

The smoothing function (LOESS) greatly effects the shape and of coverage distributions in the butterfly plot. The LOESS function (default) had the best fit, with the formula `y ~ x`.
The `span` and `length` parameters used by `geom_smooth` also impacted the fit of the model. In order to preserve the double peak of Ty1 insertion per nucleosome the span was set to `r p.span` and level was set to `r p.level`.

## Insertion rate differences between strands

### Box-and-whisker plot

Next, we wanted to learn whether there was a difference in Ty1 insertion between the positive and negative strands.

```{r strand-wise-box-and-whisker, fig.cap="Comparison of normalised read depths between the positive and negative strands.", fig.height=6, fig.width=8}

bt.strand_diff_df <- bt.cov_df %>%
  group_by(group, library, trna.name, proximity, strand, subunit, strain.type, sugar) %>%
  mutate(strand = ifelse(strand == '+',
                         "positive",
                         "negative")) %>% 
  reframe(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm))

bt.strand_diff_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = strand, y = coverage.sum, colour = proximity)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_grid(rows = vars(subunit),
             cols = vars(strain.type))+ 
  labs(x = "DNA strand",
       y = "Normalised read depth") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "")) +
  theme_bw()
```

There is no significant difference between the two strands. Coverage upstream of tRNA genes is clearly greater than downstream.

### Strand insertion at each tRNA gene

```{r strand-difference-box-and-whisker, fig.cap="Coverage difference values were calculated by subtracting the coverage of the negative strand from the coverage of the positive strand for each tRNA gene."}

bt.strand_diff_df %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = "strand",
              values_from = "coverage.sum",
              values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(strand_diff = positive - negative) %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(aes(x = group,
                      y = strand_diff,
                      colour = interaction(strain.type, sugar, sep = '+'))) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = vars(subunit),
                      scales = "free_y",
                      space = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Treatment")) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "",
                y = "Difference between positive and negative\nstrand coverage at tRNA genes") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()

```

## Mutant versus wild-type

The Ty1 retrotransposon is thought to use the RNA polymerase machinery to insert into the genome, upstream of the genes transcribed by the respective RNA polymerase enzyme -- in this case, RNA polymerase III. The RNA polymerase III subunits  [RPC160](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/RPC160), [RPC53](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/S000002309) and [RPC34](https://www.yeastgenome.org/locus/RPC34) are all necessary for transcription. To test which subunits associate with Ty1 retrotransposon's insertion machinery, each of the three subunit-encoding genes were systematically mutated and its consequent impact on insertion was analysed. A baseline of no insertion was inferred from *S. cerevisae* grown on dextrose.


```{r mutant-vs-wildtype-insertion-box-plot, fig.cap="Comparison of normalised coverage between the mutant and wild-type strains for each subunit group. For this box-plot, coverage values for only the upstream regions were used as insertion in the downstream was always less. Coverage across all tRNA genes on both strands was was summed, yielding 16 data points for each library: one for each chromosome.", fig.height=5}
bt.cov_df %>% 
  filter(proximity == "upstream") %>% 
  group_by(strain.type, sugar, subunit, trna.name, group, chr) %>% 
  reframe(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm)) %>% 
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = group,
                               y = coverage.sum,
                               colour = interaction(strain.type, sugar, sep = '+'))) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot() +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(~ subunit,
                      scales = "free_x",
                      space = "free") +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  ggplot2::guides(colour = guide_legend(title = "Treatment")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "",
                y = "Normalized 5'-most nucleotide coverage") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

```

```{r mutant-vs-wt-distribution, fig.cap="Distributions of mutant and wild-type coverage around tRNA genes. Dashed vertical lines indicate the mean coverage values for each group. Coverage was summed for each tRNA gene and library (__a__), and RNA polymerase II subunit (__b__).", fig.height=5, fig.width=13}
dist_plot.a <- bt.cov_df %>% 
  group_by(strain.type, trna.name, library) %>% 
  summarise(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm),
            .groups = "keep") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = coverage.sum,
             fill = strain.type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Normalized 5'-most nucleotide coverage",
                y = "") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = "none") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )

dist_plot.b <- bt.cov_df %>% 
  group_by(strain.type, trna.name, library, subunit) %>% 
  summarise(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm),
            .groups = "keep") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = log(coverage.sum),
             fill = strain.type,
             colour = strain.type)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(~subunit) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Log-normalized 5'-most nucleotide coverage",
                y = "") +
  stat_summary(aes(xintercept = after_stat(x),
                   y = 0),
               fun = mean, 
               geom = "vline", 
               orientation = "y",
               linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = guide_legend(title = ""),
                  colour = "none") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank()
  )

cowplot::plot_grid(dist_plot.a, dist_plot.b,
                   align = "hv",
                   labels = "auto",
                   axis = "tb",
                   rel_heights = c(1,1),
                   rel_widths = c(1, 3))
```

```{r mutant-vs-wt-t-test, tab.cap="Result of a Welch's two-sided t-test under the null hypothesis that there is no difference between the tRNA coverages of mutant and wild-type strains."}

t_test <- function(df, ...) {
  t.test(
    x = df %>% 
         dplyr::filter(strain.type == "Wild-type") %>% 
         dplyr::pull(coverage.sum), 
    y = df %>% 
         dplyr::filter(strain.type == "Mutant") %>% 
         dplyr::pull(coverage.sum),
    ...
  ) %>% 
    broom::tidy() %>% 
    dplyr::rename(
      "wt.mean"="estimate1",
      "mut.mean"="estimate2"
    ) %>% 
    return()
}

subunit_wise_t_test_helper <- function(df, ...) {
  unique_groups <- df %>%
    filter(strain.type != "Wild-type") %>% 
    pull(group) %>% 
    unique()
  
  res_cat_df <- data.frame()
  for (group_name in unique_groups) {
    res_df <- df %>% 
      filter(group == group_name | group == "WT") %>%
      t_test(df=.,
             ...) %>% 
      dplyr::mutate(group = group_name)
    if (nrow(res_cat_df) == 0)
      res_cat_df <- res_df
    else
      res_cat_df <- bind_rows(res_cat_df, res_df)
  }
  return(res_cat_df)
}

bt.cov_df %>%
  filter(sugar == "Galactose",
         subunit != "Other") %>%
  group_by(strain.type, trna.name, library, subunit, group) %>%
  summarise(coverage.sum = sum(coverage.norm),
            .groups = "keep") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    ttest = purrr::map(data,
                       subunit_wise_t_test_helper,
                       paired = FALSE,
                       conf.level = 0.99,
                       alternative = "two.sided")
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(ttest) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c("subunit", "group", "statistic", "p.value", "wt.mean", "mut.mean"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(
    digits = Inf,
    col.names = c("Subunit", "Library", "T-test statistic", "p-value", "WT mean", "Mutant mean")
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_minimal()

```

# Genome-wide Ty1 insertion site analysis

As part of the Ty1 insertion site experiments, genes in the knock-out mutants were rescued by copies on a plasmid. Since these were not located on the chromosome, however, we wanted to remove their contributions to coverage values. These regions are defined in the following table.

```{r define-blackout-regions, tab.cap="Regions removed from the coverage tables."}

feature_filter_df <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  path = p.custom_feature_file,
  sheet = "filtering"
) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(Strand = case_when(
    Strand == "positive" ~ '+',
    Strand == "negative" ~ '-',
    .default = NA
  ))

feature_filter_df %>% 
  knitr::kable() %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_minimal()

```

## Heatmap

```{r aggregate-feature-neighbourhoods}
feature_neighbourhood_list <- readxl::read_xlsx(
  path = p.custom_feature_file,
  sheet = "feature_neighbourhoods",
  col_names = c("feature.name")
) %>% 
  dplyr::pull("feature.name")

```

```{r load-heatmap-coverage-data}
hm.full_cov_df <- load_genome_coverage_data_frame(
  p.hm.cov_file,
  blackout_df = feature_filter_df,
  neighbourhoods = feature_neighbourhood_list
)

hm.cov_df <- hm.full_cov_df %>% 
  summarise_coverage_by_feature(library, feature.name)
```

The coverage values of the upstream and downstream of the following features were aggregated.

```{r check-genome-coverage-read-counts, eval=FALSE}
hm.cov_df %>% 
  group_by(library) %>% 
  reframe(total_coverage_count = sum(read_count)) %>% 
  left_join(read_counts %>% 
              .fix_library_names() %>% 
              dplyr::filter(norm_type == "Dedup"),
            by = "library") %>% 
  mutate(perc = 100 * total_coverage_count / seq_library_size) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = library, y = perc)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", alpha = 3/4, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = "",
       y = "Percentage of deduplicated reads\nin genome-wide coverage calculation") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r define-heatmap-metadata}
hm.meta_df <- hm.cov_df %>% 
  extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>% 
  dplyr::distinct(library, sugar, strain.type, subunit, group) %>% 
  tibble::column_to_rownames("library")
```


```{r plot-cov-heatmap, fig.cap = "Heatmap of genome feature mean coverage values for each library. Mean coverage was calculated by dividing the number of reads that aligned within a feature by the feature's length in base-pairs."}

for (panel in unique(hm.meta_df$subunit)) {
  draw(plot_genome_coverage_heatmap(
    cov_mat = hm.cov_df %>%
      extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>% 
      dplyr::filter(subunit == panel) %>% 
      dplyr::select(tidyselect::all_of(c("library", "feature.name", "vals"="mean_cov.norm"))) %>% 
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "feature.name",
                         values_from = "vals",
                         values_fill = 0) %>% 
      tibble::column_to_rownames("library") %>%
      t(),
    meta_df = hm.meta_df %>% 
      dplyr::filter(subunit == panel) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(group = ifelse(subunit == "Other",
                                   group,
                                   paste(subunit, group, sep = '-'))),
    annotations = c("strain.type", "sugar"),
    brewer_palette_name = c("Set1", "Set3")
  ))
}
```

writexl::write_xlsx(

## Bar-plot

```{r coverage-insertion-site-barplot-function}

plot_feature_coverage_bars <- function(df, feature_names) {
  df %>% 
    extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>% 
    dplyr::filter(
      feature.name %in% feature_names,
      sugar == "Galactose"
    ) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(
      feature.name = reorder(feature.name, mean_cov.norm),
      subunit = factor(subunit, levels = c("RPC160", "RPC34", "RPC53", "Other"))) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = feature.name, y = mean_cov.norm)) +
    geom_bar(aes(fill = group),
             stat = "identity",
             position = "dodge",
             colour = "black") +
    ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = vars(subunit),
                        cols = vars(strain.type),
                        space = "free") +
    labs(x = "Genome feature",
         y = "Mean coverage (reads/bp)") +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_fill_manual("Library",
                      values = metadata_palette_list[["group"]],
                      breaks = names(metadata_palette_list[["group"]])) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
}
```

```{r low-coverage-insertion-site-bars, fig.cap="."}

low_cov_features <- hm.cov_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(feature.name) %>% 
  dplyr::reframe(median_cov = median(mean_cov.norm)) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(median_cov) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(median_cov < 5E-3) %>% 
  dplyr::pull(feature.name)

plot_feature_coverage_bars(
  df = hm.cov_df,
  feature_names = low_cov_features)
```

# Appendix

## Ty1 insertion quantification at tRNA genes

### RPC160 butterfly plots

These are to show side-by-side comparisons of RPC160 mutants to wild-type 

```{r rpc160-butterfly-panel, fig.height=14, fig.width=10, fig.cap="Butterfly plots of the RPC160 mutants compared to the wild-type."}

plot_mutant_and_wildtype_butterfly_helper <- function(df) {
  panel <- list()
  i <- 1
  mutant_libs <- df %>% 
    filter(strain.type == "Mutant") %>% 
    pull(library) %>% 
    unique()
  
  for (library_name in mutant_libs) {
    panel[[i]] <- df %>%
      dplyr::filter(library == library_name | strain.type == "Wild-type",
                    sugar == "Galactose") %>%
      plot_butterfly(df = .,
                     trna_feat_df = trna_df,
                     annot_df = nucleosome_position_df,
                     span = p.span,
                     level = p.level,
                     .smooth_se = TRUE,
                     .annot_size = 4) +
      theme(
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank()
      ) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(6, "Set3"),
                                            mutant_libs))
    i <- i + 1
  }
  
  cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist = panel,
                     ncol = 1)
}

bt.cov_df %>%
  filter(subunit == "RPC160") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(subunit, strain.type, sugar, library, proximity, strand, rel.position) %>%
  summarise(
    coverage.norm = sum(coverage.norm),
    .groups = "keep"
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>%
  plot_mutant_and_wildtype_butterfly_helper()

```

## Genome-wide Ty1 insertion site analysis

```{r low-coverage-features, fig.cap="Bar-plot with error bars representing the mean coverage (in reads per base-pair) of each feature across. Libraries grown on destrose were excluded from this figure so as to not bias the summary functions."}

hm.cov_df %>%
  extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>% 
  dplyr::filter(
    feature.name %in% low_cov_features,
    sugar == "Galactose"
  ) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(feature.name = reorder(feature.name, mean_cov.norm)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = feature.name, y = mean_cov.norm)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "summary") +
  geom_errorbar(stat = "summary",
                width = 0.5) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = vars(subunit),
                      cols = vars(strain.type)) +
  labs(x = "Genome feature",
       y = "Mean coverage (reads/bp)") +
  theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```


### TPM heatmap


```{r plot-tpm-heatmap, fig.cap = "Heatmap of genome feature mean TPM values for each library."}
plot_genome_coverage_heatmap(
  cov_mat = hm.cov_df %>%
    dplyr::select(tidyselect::all_of(c("library", "feature.name", "vals"="mean_tpm"))) %>% 
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "feature.name",
                       values_from = "vals",
                       values_fill = 0) %>% 
    tibble::column_to_rownames("library") %>%
    t(),
  meta_df = hm.meta_df,
  annotations = c("strain.type", "sugar", "subunit"),
  brewer_palette_name = c("Set1", "Set3", "Accent"),
  legend_title = "Mean\nTPM"
)
```


### Mean TPM and coverage relationship

The following figure is to determine how the choice between TPM and coverage influences the results and potentially the interpretation.

```{r cov-tpm-scatter-plot, fig.cap="Mean coverage and TPM values are linearly correlated, and the slope of the relationship is explained by the library.", fig.height=4, fig.width=10}
hm.cov_df %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_cov, y = mean_tpm, colour = library)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme_bw()
```

The figure above shows that there is less differentiation between the different libraries when using TPM values (y-axis) compared to using coverage values (x-axis). Whether this reflects true signal or a lack of normalization in calculating coverage values is not clear.


### Coverage using unique alignments

```{r plot-uniq-cov-heatmap, fig.cap = "Heatmap of genome feature mean coverage values for each library - for unambiguous alignments. Mean coverage was calculated by dividing the number of reads that aligned within a feature by the feature's length in base-pairs. Alignments that mapped ambiguously to multiple regions were removed."}
hm.uniq_cov_df <- load_genome_coverage_data_frame(file_path = p.hm.uniq_cov_file,
                                                  blackout_df = feature_filter_df,
                                                  neighbourhoods = feature_neighbourhood_list) %>%
  summarise_coverage_by_feature(library, feature.name)

for (panel in unique(hm.meta_df$subunit)) {
  draw(plot_genome_coverage_heatmap(
    cov_mat = hm.uniq_cov_df %>%
      extract_metadata_from_library_names() %>% 
      dplyr::filter(subunit == panel) %>% 
      dplyr::select(tidyselect::all_of(c("library", "feature.name", "vals"="mean_cov.norm"))) %>% 
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "feature.name",
                         values_from = "vals",
                         values_fill = 0) %>% 
      tibble::column_to_rownames("library") %>%
      t(),
    meta_df = hm.meta_df %>% 
      dplyr::filter(subunit == panel) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(group = ifelse(subunit == "Other",
                                   group,
                                   paste(subunit, group, sep = '-'))),
    annotations = c("strain.type", "sugar"),
    brewer_palette_name = c("Set1", "Set3")
  ))
}
```

trna_features <- hm.cov_df %>%
